bib.title: 3. Making an Intelligent Application Agentic with MCP Clients (AI Agents with MCP, early release)

question: How do you build an MCP host application and client that connects to a server and uses its tools, resources and prompts with an LLM?
contributions: Walk-through of a minimal host (chat loop on Anthropic Messages API) and an MCPClient class with stdio and Streamable HTTP connect/disconnect
Wrapper patterns for tools, resources and prompts with guardrails and logging
Host integrations: tool-use loop, LLM-based resource selection as context, LLM-based prompt selection as system instructions

results.claim: Agent performance tends to drop dramatically as more tools are added, attributed to harder tool selection from overlapping descriptions and too much aggregate description content.
results.quote: Performance tends to drop dramatically as more tools are added, typically due to an increased difficulty in selecting the correct tool for a prompt.

results.claim: The example resource/prompt selection costs one extra LLM call per user input (max_tokens 200 each).
results.quote: currently, our application does 1 extra potentially expensive LLM csll for each user input in order to select the most relevant resources for the user’s query.

limits: Early-release draft; no authors printed in the capture, no empirical data.

The captured text ends after the prompts example. The introduction promises multiple-server tradeoffs, authentication, resource filtering, model agnosticism and best practices (security, reliability, responsiveness), but none appear; the TOC suggests best practices are in Ch 4.
Code is truncated in the PDF capture (lines cut mid-statement); some code is not runnable as shown (e.g. await in non-async main).
Notification handling (list_changed, resource subscribe) only partly supported in the Python SDK as of writing; MCP connector beta tools-only.
Dated: SDK APIs, Claude model names (claude-sonnet-4-0), SSE superseded by Streamable HTTP.
practices: Build a client class wrapping the SDK session; minimum is connect, discover, make available to LLM (Basic Client Design).
Wrap list/call methods with connection checks, logging, empty-result warnings, and optional cursor pagination (Tools).
Do not pass all system env vars to a stdio server via env_vars, it can expose secrets (stdio).
Secure remote transports: authenticate and validate origin headers (Streamable HTTP warning).
Never commit .env files with API keys (host example warning).
Convert MCP Tool objects to the LLM API's schema (name, description, input_schema); refresh the tool list per input or listen for list_changed if tools can change.
Monitor tool-calling performance as tools are added.
Add resource context as extra content blocks in the user message, not a separate user message (Resources note).
Resources are for extra context; prompts are user-controlled templates with arguments, injected here as system instructions; filter hallucinated prompt/resource names returned by the selector LLM.
Roots are not enforced; servers must honour them and users should vet servers.

terms.definition: anything that hosts the client(s) managing connections to MCP servers and communicates with an LLM
handles all communication and connections to a server; connections are one-to-one
an implementation of the protocol's transport layer, managing how messages are sent between client and server (stdio, Streamable HTTP)
boundaries (such as a filesystem location) within which connecting servers should operate; not strictly enforced
prompts whose arguments are injected by the client or host
